author: AntiTrace
text_post: I agree to an extent. I have been in the American Army for almost 8 years. I have definitely become more confident, remained in shape, had a decent income, and picked up some pretty good stories to tell.  It will make you tolerate less bullshit and play less games, but so will learning any aspect of game. It will keep in shape, but not much more than any other civilian. There are plenty of pigs running around in a uniform. It can give you a DHV, if you have earned it. Most people have shitty little jobs in the army, and try to talk like they are rambo. I destroy these people when I hear them by picking apart their stories and making it is evident they dont know shit. Almost all the people that I know that have actually been in combat (actually in firefights on the ground, not just deployed to a combat zone) only talk about with others that have done the same thing. Most military are not DHV status, simple as that. You can travel, but say goodbye to traveling on your own. I get a month of leave a year, normally broken down into two seperate 15 day breaks. One in the summer and one in the winter (xmas). Other than that, you will not be able to travel. Most posts have a 150-250 mile limit that you are not allowed to travel outside without special permission. It can also seriously fuck your head up. I went through about a two year window where I was terrified of women. I was convinced anything I did would make them scream rape or sexual harassment, and my career would be over. However, I still think it the best decision a young American can make. If your not pursuing a degree in a highly specialized high income field, or running your own business, the military is mint for long term financial stability and upward career mobility. If you are a go getter you can land yourself in military programs that train you in high demand skills for free, while paying you do it. Finish up your obligation after schooling (normally 4-6 years depending on the program) and either stay in for the sweet retirement, or get out and goto the civilian sector. The military will abuse every aspect of your body and soul when you are serving, so do it right back and take advantage of every single opportunity and cent that you can squeeze out of them.
